title: Here’s why one market bull says betting on innovation is still a slam dunk - MarketWatch
text:
Read: U.K. delays Brexit vote — what happens next?
Check out the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
Europe SXXP, +1.53% is marching higher, while it was a mixed session in Asia, where the Nikkei NIK, -0.34% had another down day . The chart
When retail investors get super gloomy about stocks, look out above, say some. Our chart of the day , from the Investor Movement Index (via The Wall Street Journal’s Daily Shot ) shows just how negative Main Street was for November:
Granted, November was a heck of a month. Sidle on over to the AAII Sentiment Survey and the first week of December looks a little split when it comes to bulls, bears and those who can’t decide. Check out more so-called contrarian indexes here .
Read: OECD economist says prepare for the worst when it comes to the global economy The buzz
Auto shares are moving higher premarket — Ford F, +0.23% and GM GM, +0.78% — as Bloomberg reports the Chinese government is reviewing a proposal to cut tariffs on U.S. made autos to 15% from 40%. They’re jumping ahead in Europe too.
The latest round of U.S.-China trade talks kicked off late Monday with a call between Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and Chinese Vice Premier Liu He. Meanwhile, a bail hearing for a jailed Huawei executive has been delayed by a day . Some say her arrest has put a “bull’s-eye” on Apple .
Speaking of, Apple’s AAPL, -0.57% miserable performance since September could mean trouble for Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway BRK.A, -0.45% , BRK.B, -0.48% says Barron’s . As Berkshire’s biggest holding, the conglomerate has lost about $15 billion so far this quarter just on that holding.
Delta DAL, -0.76% is banning support animals on flights over 8 hours, and puppies and kittens are totally off limits. The airline says it has seen a spike in incidents involving service animals in the last two years.
Amazon AMZN, +0.13% is making its own chips, and that could be bad news for Intel INTC, +0.36% according to the New York Times.
Embattled U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May will meet with EU President Donald Tusk later to talk Brexit after she delayed a potentially brutal parliament vote that had been skedded for Tuesday.
On the economy beat, a small-business sentiment index hit a seven-month low for November . Producer prices are still to come. The quote Reuters Youths and students demonstrate a day after Macron’s speech in Paris, Dec. 11
“My only concern is you, my only combat is for you – our only battle is for France.” — That was French President Emmanuel Macron in a public address late Monday as he attempted to quell civil unrest in his country that has been particularly bad in places like Paris. He offered tax cuts and minimum wage boost to the so-called “gilets jaunes” (yellow jackets), many of whom see him as a “president of the rich.”
Publicis PUB, +1.31% and Altice ATUS, -0.11% are two companies that have announced bonuses for some French employees in the wake of the protests and Macron’s speech. Random reads

A plea deal may have been reached for an alleged Russian agent.
Nuns on a gambling spree . No, really.
